hypothesis: At the exact conservative TeaCache round-6 threshold and one-hit cap, a faithful branch-specific first-order TaylorSeer forecast can be compared on an equal schedule and measured time to determine whether it improves the lightweight visual screen without losing the conservative speed point.

build.tests: 9/9 CPU tests passed; branch-specific Taylor history/forecast, ledger validation, dry-run, git diff, exact lease UUID, GPU-idle, and shared-lock availability preflights passed. The optional DeepGEMM warning remained benign.

run.signal_definition: relative mean-L1 change of token-subsampled first-block AdaLN-modulated hidden input, accumulated with identity rescaling
run.reuse_payload: separate conditional and unconditional first-order forecasts from independent residual histories

validity.visual_note: The first/middle/last frames preserve identity, anatomy, forest composition, and flare progression without gross artifacts. TaylorSeer may be subtly closer to dense in framing/pose than TeaCache round 6, but the approved one-prompt screen does not support a decisive quality-superiority claim; the two are effectively tied at this conservative schedule.

decision.reason: Retain as the conservative matched-time TaylorSeer comparator: the exact eight-hit schedule matches TeaCache round 6, 46.9 s is within 0.428% of Tea and 1.515% of EasyCache round 2, and the lightweight visual screen passes. No decisive quality win over Tea is claimed.
